content.value_statement: Preview SDK changes make Cloudflare Sandbox applications difficult to implement correctly. This skill provides version-specific contracts, examples, and official documentation routes.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether Worker packages and container images use the same @next release line.
Explains process handles, output collection, readiness checks, timeouts, and termination.
Provides a minimal TypeScript pattern for creating a sandbox and launching a process.
Routes process, terminal, interpreter, lifecycle, environment, and error tasks to official documentation.
Highlights preview-specific API differences and removed stable APIs.
limitations: Supports @cloudflare/sandbox@next, not the default stable package.
Does not provide a complete API reference.
Does not migrate stable applications to the preview release.
Requires checking installed types because preview APIs can change.

use_cases.title: Create a Preview Sandbox Worker
use_cases.description: Start a Worker with matching preview dependencies, container images, and process handling.

use_cases.title: Review Sandbox Process Logic
use_cases.description: Check command launch, output collection, readiness, timeout, and termination behavior.

use_cases.title: Design an AI Code Runner
use_cases.description: Choose process, terminal, or interpreter APIs for isolated agent workloads.

prompt_templates.title: Confirm Preview Compatibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this project for @cloudflare/sandbox@next compatibility. Identify package and container version mismatches before suggesting changes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Process Execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a sandbox process that runs these fixed arguments, waits for completion, and reports output and exit status.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Interactive Terminal
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an interactive terminal with createTerminal and connect. Explain lifecycle, reconnection, and termination behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Durable Runner
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this runner for container replacement, stale process identifiers, secret exposure, timeout handling, and preview API compatibility.

output_examples.input: Explain why my command returns before output is available.
output_examples.output: The launch returns a process handle after startup. Read output or wait for exit through the handle.

output_examples.input: Review my stable package with a preview container image.
output_examples.output: The package and image lines conflict. Use matching stable components or move both components to the preview line.

output_examples.input: Where should sandboxed code receive an external API credential?
output_examples.output: Keep the live credential in the Worker. Route sandbox requests through an outbound handler instead of placing secrets in sandbox environment variables.

best_practices: Match the Worker package, lockfile, and container image release lines.
Check installed preview types and current documentation before implementing.
Keep live credentials in the Worker and use outbound handlers.
anti_patterns: Do not mix stable packages with preview container images.
Do not treat process launch as process completion.
Do not reuse stable-only APIs or store only transient process identifiers.

faq.question: Does this skill support the stable Sandbox SDK?
faq.answer: No. Use the sandbox-stable skill for the default package.

faq.question: Can this skill migrate a stable application?
faq.answer: No. Use sandbox-migrate-to-next for migration work.

faq.question: Does sandbox.exec return completed output?
faq.answer: No. It returns a process handle after launch. Use handle methods to collect output or wait.

faq.question: Can process handles accept interactive input?
faq.answer: No. Use a terminal with createTerminal and connect for interactive sessions.

faq.question: Should secrets be placed in sandbox environment variables?
faq.answer: No. Keep live credentials in the Worker and use outbound handlers.

faq.question: Are the included API notes complete?
faq.answer: No. Consult installed @next types and current Cloudflare documentation for complete signatures.
